study_identification_part.si4_title: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Step-by-step evaluation: (1) Research hypotheses/questions are provided - YES: The study clearly states hypotheses about multimodal components being more sensitive to capturing diagnostic effects and outperforming unimodal components in discriminating autistic from nonautistic individuals, and that joint expression across modalities would specifically inform social functioning in autism. (2) The purpose of applying normative modeling is described - YES: The paper explicitly states the purpose is to characterize multimodal neural signatures of face processing in autism, identify individual-level deviations from normative trajectories, and link these to clinical features for potential biomarker identification and personalized support. Both criteria are satisfied, leading to a 'Yes' answer.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "In the present study, our aim was to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the FFG in face processing in autism by elucidating the simultaneous involvement and multivariate interplay of different neural sources."; "We hypothesized that multimodal components, by leveraging joint effects across different biological processes, would be more sensitive to capturing subtle diagnostic effects cross-modally. Consequently, they would outperform unimodal components in discriminating autistic from NAI. Finally, we hypothesized that joint expression across modalities related to the FFG and face processing would specifically inform social functioning in autism."; "elucidating more precise, integrated and individual-level neural associations of core cognitive and clinical features will pave the way for further work identifying stratification, mechanistic and prognostic biomarkers and the development of more personalized support"
